He also said that the recent row over the Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie's top job was "manufactured in Paris and Kinshasa". Finally, he defended a deal for Rwanda to host failed asylum seekers from five European countries.

items.title: 🔴Anthropic soars more than 30% to $2 trillion valuation on first day of trading
How much do businesses want to pay for AI?
items.desc: Four years after ChatGPT went mainstream, generative AI is transforming how we live and work. It's also been a major driver of economic growth, with massive amounts of money poured into expanding global computing capacity. But now, there are signs of a slowdown in AI spending as companies take a reality check: are they getting sufficient returns on their investments and how much artificial intelligence do they actually need?

items.title: Inside France's mental health crisis: Are the French all right?
items.desc: This week, we try to get inside the heads of French people, with a deep dive into mental health in France. For a nation that loves analysing its problems, its mental health figures make for sobering reading: nearly one in five French people are affected by a mental health issue.

items.title: ICJ ruling on Myanmar genocide: ‘Historic victory for Rohingya, landmark for international justice’
items.desc: Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Reed Brody, Member of the International Commission of Jurists, Human Rights Lawyer and veteran war crimes prosecutor. The International Court of Justice's ruling on Myanmar marks, according to Brody, "a historic victory for the Rohingya, but also a landmark for international justice." He explains how the court assessed evidence of genocidal intent, rejecting Myanmar's justification of its military operations as counterterrorism. He argues that "the existence of an armed conflict or a security objective doesn't exclude genocidal intent," a finding he believes will have "far-reaching implications in future genocide cases," including South Africa's case against Israel over Gaza. Brody also discusses the Gambia's role in bringing the case and growing challenges to international accountability, warning that "we're in a very dangerous moment."

items.title: Xi demonstrating China's 'global status', occupying 'central position' in relation to Trump & Putin
items.desc: Sharon Gaffney is pleased to welcome Rex Li, professor of international relations at King's College London. For Professor Li, the meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in China is less about "reaching concrete agreements and a common position." Rather, he argues, it is about demonstrating Xi's ability to bring the American and Russian leaders together to discuss major geopolitical issues. Li believes that Xi Jinping has the most to gain from the meeting, as it allows him to demonstrate China's global status and its role as a diplomatic convener. Putin may also benefit from the opportunity to meet the two leaders despite Russia's international isolation following its invasion of Ukraine.

items.title: Gender pay gap: French women work "for free” from today
items.desc: Women in Europe are still paid less than men, with the gap falling from 15.1% in 2016 to 11.1% in 2024, according to Eurostat. In France, women symbolically start working for free from 10:51 am on Thursday, 19 November, and at the current pace equality would not be reached until 2062. Experts warn that AI could make things worse by eliminating administrative and legal jobs where many women work, while childbirth and short paternity leave continue to slow women’s careers.

items.title: 'GTA VI': A masterpiece? Fans react to gaming's biggest release
items.desc: Critics are calling the new "Grand Theft Auto VI" a masterpiece. In this edition of arts24, we hear what fans make of one of the biggest video game releases in history. We also look at U2's new album and tour marking 50 years of the band, discover the French comic book that Pope Leo is reading and meet the women redefining Mexico's Mariachi tradition.

items.title: The chocolate countdown: The art of the advent calendar
items.desc: The holiday season is almost upon us and with it come advent calendars. The annual physical countdown originated in 19th-century Germany as a Christian tradition to count down the days until Christmas. Eugénie Pont from the magazine Fou de Pâtisserie tells us more about what we can expect from the biggest chocolate makers in France.

items.title: Trump, Xi, Putin summit: What was it all about?
items.desc: Donald Trump has left China after a historic first meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Ukraine was discussed without Kyiv or European leaders in the room, which raised eyebrows, though Trump defended dialogue with rivals and Putin said the talks created conditions for future agreements. Xi warned major powers against conflict, and topics included reducing nuclear risks, reforming the UN and increasing energy flows.

items.title: Behind the UK's use of AI in asylum applications
items.desc: The UK is increasingly turning to artificial intelligence to manage its immigration system, from analysing migrants’ phones to processing asylum applications. But what happens when AI gets involved in deciding how an asylum seeker's story is understood? Stella Elgersma, journalist at InfoMigrants, explains how the UK Home Office is testing AI tools to process asylum applications, including a system that generates summaries of asylum interviews. With errors, limited human oversight and concerns over transparency, could AI put asylum seekers’ lives at risk?

items.title: Haiti: Salvador’s Bukele publishes video of attack on gang leader’s house
items.desc: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele said Wednesday that his troops demolished the lavish home of a prominent gang leader in Haiti known as Jeff Gwo Lwa. "My gift to the Haitian people on the anniversary of the Battle of Vertières," Bukele wrote on X - referencing a 1803 battle critical in helping secure Haiti's independence from France.

items.title: Beaujolais Nouveau: A French tradition uncorked
items.desc: Every year on the third Thursday of November, France raises a glass to one of its most joyful traditions: Le Beaujolais Nouveau! That means that this Thursday, millions of bottles of the 2026 young red wine will be uncorked around the world, from Lyon to New York. Olivier Badoureaux, wine expert and director of the French trade organisation Inter Beaujolais, tells us what we should expect from this year's vintage.

items.title: France: Retirees march against 2027 budget cuts
items.desc: More than a thousand people marched in Paris on Thursday, called by a union alliance joined by student and high-school groups, to protest social and tax measures targeting retirees in the 2027 budgets. The government wants retirees to contribute about €5.4 billion, by freezing the indexation of pensions above €1,260 and reforming their 10% income tax allowance. Union leaders say the money should not come from retirees’ pockets, as FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago explains.

items.title: 🔴 AI firm Anthropic begins trading on Nasdaq, aiming to raise $81 billion in biggest IPO on record
Anthropic blows past $2 trillion in Nasdaq debut, beating SpaceX's June listing
items.desc: Anthropic hit $2 trillion in market value as its shares soared in their Nasdaq debut on Thursday, with investors rushing to own a stake in the maker of the Claude chatbot, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company. Shares began trading at $111.5, 34% higher than the IPO price of $83.

items.title: Chef Rachel Khoo: 'You don't need fancy kitchen gadgets to cook delicious food'
items.desc: One of the world's best-known chefs has spoken to FRANCE 24 about her new book that proves you certainly don't need fancy kitchen gadgets to cook delicious meals. The book "The Smallest Restaurant in Paris" tells her own story of starting out in a tiny Parisian flat cooking food just for two people at a time. That then led to a BBC series and a decade of writing and filming cooking stories. Rachel Khoo is now a judge on "The Great Australian Bake Off". She spoke to us in Perspective.

items.title: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
items.desc: In August 2017, after attacks by a Rohingya militia, Myanmar’s army launched a “clearance campaign” in Rakhine state, with survivors describing mass killings, rapes and burned villages as hundreds of thousands fled to Bangladesh. The Gambia took Myanmar to the ICJ in 2019, and after a seven-year legal fight the court has ruled that Myanmar committed acts of genocide. Meanwhile some 1.2 million Rohingya remain in crowded camps, unable to return home.

items.title: China summit ends with little new, Europe backs Ukraine in Berlin
items.desc: The leaders of China, the United States and Russia met in Shenzhen for a historic first, but the summit brought little new: non-binding statements on peace and no plan to meet regularly. In Berlin, Europeans gathered to show their support for Ukraine, a pointed answer to a summit where Europe had no seat, as FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

items.title: In South Korea, women forced into prostitution on US military bases seek justice
items.desc: Tens of thousands of women were forced to work in South Korean state-sanctioned brothels used by American soldiers based in the country after the Korean War. They were raped, physically abused and forcibly confined. Now, after decades of silence, some of these women are speaking out.

items.title: 货币基金组织总裁：人工智能将成为影响全球竞争力和经济增长的重要因素
items.desc: 国际货币基金组织总裁格奥尔基耶娃周四在中国深圳举行的2026年亚太经合组织经济领导人会议上表示，人工智能正在对全球经济增长产生实质性影响，将成为影响中期竞争力、生产率和经济增长的重要因素。她同时指出，全球通胀上升、公共债务增加以及结构性改革滞后等问题仍对经济前景构成挑战，各国需要加快采取政策行动。

items.title: 联合国人口基金警告：世界正面临辜负下一代的风险
items.desc: 联合国人口基金周三发布的《2026年世界人口状况报告》指出，尽管年轻一代的教育水平、信息获取能力以及对自身权利的认知达到前所未有的高度，但经济不稳定、不平等、排斥、冲突和气候变化等因素，正阻碍数以百万计的年轻人实现人生抱负，使他们难以获得体面的工作、经济独立、住房以及建立家庭的机会。

items.title: 第31届气候变化大会僵局持续，各国启动新一轮“气候承诺核查”
items.desc: 随着在土耳其安塔利亚举行的第31届联合国气候变化大会闭幕时限日益临近，各国于周三启动了一项新的全球性核查，以检验气候承诺是否得到履行。与此同时，各国部长在峰会的一些最棘手问题上仍陷于僵局：谁来买单、全球摆脱化石燃料的速度有多快，以及如果较贫穷国家无力承担，更绿色的未来能否被称为“公正”。

items.title: 经巴拿马北上人流减少九成，拉美移民转向新路线
items.desc: 国际移民组织周三发布报告指出，2026年上半年，经巴拿马达连隘口北上的移民人数较去年同期下降90%。与此同时，部分移民转而南下、返乡或在其他国家定居，拉丁美洲和加勒比地区的迁徙路线与目的地正在发生变化。

items.title: COP31：海洋保护进入谈判议程，落实承诺仍需资金支持
items.desc: 第31届联合国气候变化大会（COP31）周二聚焦海洋与自然保护。科学家和社区代表展示了利用海水样本监测生物、借鉴土著知识预防野火等办法，但资金不足仍阻碍这些措施得到落实。随着大会进入最后几天，各国也在加紧磋商，争取在化石燃料和气候资金等关键问题上达成共识。

items.title: 苏丹：联合国报告详述无人机袭击激增对平民造成的致命影响
